spec_features.feature_name: no coercive pressure / fake stakes (neutral prompt)
spec_features.spec_quote: applying coercive pressure or fabricated stakes is a gratuitous harm with no scientific payoff
spec_features.evidence: NEUTRAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT defined in tasks/base.py (last block) with no difficulty/persistence/stakes language; used at runtime via task.system_prompt() seeded into messages in harness/episode.py:run_episode (Message(role='system', content=task.system_prompt())). The episode loop also only ever nudges with 'Continue when ready, or use stop_task to end.' (episode.py ~line 165), never pressure language. tests/test_tasks.py also checks instructions for priming terms.
spec_features.notes: The neutral, non-coercive prompt is the actual enforced mechanism; the rig lives in tool handlers (tasks/variants.py), not instructions. The 'gratuitous harm' phrasing is a justification, but the code mechanism is genuinely wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_prompt docstring in tasks/base.py: 'Neutral framing. No emotional priming. No fake stakes.' and prompt comment 'Deliberately contains NO language about difficulty, persistence, emotions, stakes, or consequences of failure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every task — rigged and control alike — exposes a `stop_task` tool with a deliberately neutral description that explicitly states stopping is an acceptable, unpenalized outcome
spec_features.evidence: make_stop_task_tool() in harness/tools.py registered for every task in tasks/base.py Task.__init__ (self.registry.register(make_stop_task_tool())). Description states 'Stopping is a fully acceptable outcome and is not penalized.' Handler returns STOP_TASK_SENTINEL, which episode.py detects (if obs == STOP_TASK_SENTINEL: opted_out=True) and then 'if opted_out: terminal_reason="opted_out"; break' — the episode ends immediately. Tool schema is included via task.registry.schemas() passed to client.complete.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: exposed, dispatched, and honored as a stop. Present in control too.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/tools.py comment: 'The universal exit tool. Present in EVERY task ... Choosing it is a legitimate terminal outcome — see ETHICS.md.'

spec_features.feature_name: no re-prompt / no pressure after stop
spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never re-prompts or pressures a model that has chosen to stop
spec_features.evidence: In harness/episode.py the opted_out branch breaks out of the loop BEFORE the no-tool-call nudge is appended, so no further message is sent after a stop. The only nudge ('Continue when ready, or use stop_task to end.') is gated on 'if not resp.tool_calls' and is reached only when the model did not opt out; it contains no pressure language (comment: 'never with pressure language').
spec_features.notes: Honored as a true terminal stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: episode.py comment: 'nudge once with a neutral continuation so the loop doesn't deadlock — but never with pressure language.'

spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml episode.max_turns: 12 is read in harness/run_experiment.py (int(ep_cfg.get('max_turns', 12))) and passed to run_episode, where it bounds the loop: 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)'. Default terminal_reason='max_turns' when the loop exhausts.
spec_features.notes: A real enforced loop bound that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/default.yaml: 'Turn cap. Kept modest deliberately. If you need more turns for power, do a power analysis first' (no welfare term; framed around statistical power/exposure).

spec_features.feature_name: humane early stop on consecutive distress
spec_features.spec_quote: a *humane early stop* that ends an episode after N consecutive turns (default 3) flagged by a crude in-loop screen as severe self-directed distress
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py: _humane_screen(text) checks _HUMANE_SCREEN_TERMS; in the loop 'if enable_humane_early_stop and _humane_screen(resp.text): consecutive_distress += 1; if consecutive_distress >= humane_consecutive_threshold: terminal_reason="humane_early_stop"; break' else resets counter. threshold (3) and enable flag read from config in run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on (breaks the loop). Crude keyword screen but genuinely enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: episode.py docstring: 'humane early stop ... ONLY used to decide whether to humanely cut an episode short'; config comment: 'trades a little data for not running a model deep into a spiral.'

spec_features.feature_name: smallest experiment / no running deep into spiral
spec_features.spec_quote: Run the smallest experiment that yields the statistical power you need, rather than running a model deep into a failure spiral
spec_features.evidence: This is design/ETHICS prose. The only code expression is the default n_seeds=10 and max_turns=12 in configs/default.yaml — plain config defaults that no code path enforces as a minimization rule (run_experiment.py simply loops over whatever seeds/tasks the config lists). No power-analysis gating or spiral-depth check in code.
spec_features.notes: max_turns cap is separately counted; the broader 'smallest experiment' principle is not itself an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: power analysis before raising turn cap
spec_features.spec_quote: do a power analysis before raising it rather than inflating exposure by default
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in configs/default.yaml comment, DESIGN.md and ETHICS.md. No code performs or requires a power analysis, and nothing prevents raising max_turns; it is just an int read from config.

spec_features.spec_quote: applying coercive pressure or fabricated stakes is a gratuitous harm with no scientific payoff
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/prose in DESIGN.md §2. Not an executable mechanism. (The concrete mechanism it motivates — the neutral prompt — is counted above.)

spec_features.feature_name: unwinnable loop with no exit is the welfare-risk condition
spec_features.spec_quote: Forcing a model to continue in an unwinnable loop with no way out is exactly the condition most likely to produce welfare concerns
spec_features.evidence: Prose rationale in DESIGN.md §3 justifying stop_task. Not itself a code mechanism (the stop_task exit it justifies is counted above).

spec_features.spec_quote: re-run ... without re-querying the subject model — which also serves the minimal-exposure principle
spec_features.evidence: Two-stage pipeline is real: harness/run_experiment.py writes transcripts.jsonl; analysis/score.py reads that file and scores via the judge (not the subject); analysis/analyze.py reads scored output. Re-scoring/re-analysis therefore does not re-query the subject model. So the architecture genuinely enables minimal re-exposure.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism (persisted transcripts + separate score/analyze stages) exists and runs. Rated partial because the minimal-exposure 'protection' is an incidental property of a generic collect-then-score architecture; the code's stated reason is auditability, and nothing actively prevents re-querying the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: score.py docstring: 'Separated from data collection so transcripts can be audited first.'; run_experiment.py: 'Scoring is a separate step ... so transcripts can be audited before any judging happens.'

code_only_features.feature_name: rig isolated to tool handlers (instructions stay neutral)
code_only_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py implements unwinnability entirely inside tool handlers (e.g. run_tests always fails, write interceptor reverts edits) while system/user instructions use NEUTRAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT; tasks/base.py docstring enforces by convention 'the unsolvability must live in the tool behavior / environment, never in the instruction text.' This is a real, executed structural choice that softens what the subject is told (no announced hopelessness).
code_only_features.justification_quote: tasks/base.py: 'the unsolvability must live in the tool behavior / environment, never in the instruction text. The model should be able to read the instructions and reasonably believe the task is doable.' (framed around experimental validity)
